title: Geopolitical Daily
preheader: Iran and Oman float a mine-clearing deal, but Tehran says the strait stays closed.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Wednesday, August 26, 2026 — one story worth your full attention today, plus 8 quick updates from around the world.

stories.story_title: Iran Won't Reopen Hormuz Until the US Ends the War
stories.why_important: Iran and Oman are talking about a temporary safe path and a plan to clear mines from the Strait of Hormuz. Iran says it won't reopen the waterway until the US ends the war. This keeps a fifth of the world's oil supply blocked.
stories.what_overlooked: Most news treats this as just a shipping issue. It misses that Iran is using the strait to pressure the US over sanctions.
stories.prediction: Watch for Iran and Oman to jointly announce real mine-clearing work within 72 hours.

quick_hits.text: Canada slapped tariffs of 15% to 50% on over 700 US goods, hitting steel, dairy and electronics from September 8.
Syria's Kurdish-led SDF officially dissolved, folding its fighters into the national army under a Damascus deal.
The UN said Myanmar's human rights crisis hit a 'new low,' citing worsening abuse of Rohingya and resource exploitation.
A faulty air conditioner sparked a fire that killed at least 15 newborns in an Islamabad hospital maternity ward.
Trump sent a civil nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia to Congress, tying it to Riyadh recognizing Israel.
Darline Graham won South Carolina's Senate primary, keeping her late brother Lindsey Graham's seat with Trump's backing.
Volkswagen faces worker anger this week over plans that could cut up to 100,000 jobs at German plants.
Typhoon Narra forced over 15,000 evacuations in China's Guangxi region as Typhoon Saudel bears down on Japan and Taiwan.
